findings.issue: Technical passes use vague news-dependent reconsideration
findings.evidence: ETH, HYPE, CC and LIT new-prompt decisions require material attributable supply/demand without a concrete observation defining reversal. ETH/CC/LIT created material_news watches; HYPE retained prior monitoring. Across the day, 80 set_watch calls chose pass/material_news (calls, not unique watches).
findings.interpretation: Cash may be justified; the documented reassessment condition is not sufficiently testable. A news trigger does not directly test the stated technical persistence question.

findings.issue: CHIP cover-side depth described as an enforced short-entry blocker
findings.evidence: 16:24:43 CET archived quote: bids $5,760.07, asks $2,045.01, both complete in band. Lead described asks below $2,500 as independently blocking the short.
findings.code: execution-risk.ts uses depth.levels[buy ? 1 : 0] for entry minDepthUsd; size_swing_trade likewise uses bids for sell entries.
findings.interpretation: Thin cover liquidity can justify a discretionary pass, but it is distinct from failing the host short-entry depth check.

findings.issue: One real entry preference was reached under the old prompt
findings.evidence: 14:09 CET XMR action=enter, quantity 0.581, notional $302.67, planned risk $6.09745 within headroom-adjusted $6.1005. Preview returned Order violates slippage limit. Fresh quote subsequently crossed the saved $518.28 retention boundary; lead changed to pass before sending an order.
findings.interpretation: The book risk budget was not what blocked this attempt; the preview and subsequent evidence change matter.
